NSE:GRANULES.name: Granules India Ltd
NSE:GRANULES.businessSummary: Hyderabad-based pharma manufacturer of finished dosage forms, formulation intermediates and APIs, focused on high-volume off-patent products (paracetamol, metformin, ibuprofen) sold to 300+ customers in 80+ countries across regulated US/EU markets.

notes.announcementTitle: Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Press Release / Media Release
notes.insight: Granules secured Sole First-to-File (FTF) ANDA status for Sodium Oxybate Extended-Release for Oral Suspension, the generic of LUMRYZ (a narcolepsy/cataplexy drug). This is the companys second Sole FTF ANDA after Amphetamine ER Tablets (generic Dyanavel XR), signalling growing capability in complex, differentiated generics rather than commodity products. Sole FTF status typically confers 180-day marketing exclusivity in the US on approval, which can be materially margin-accretive versus Granules base paracetamol/metformin business, but the PDF gives no revenue estimate, approval timeline, or launch date — actual P&L impact is unquantifiable from this filing alone. No prior notes exist for this company to compare against. Watch for: FDA approval/launch timing and management commentary on expected US market size for this molecule in the next concall.
notes.announcementDescription: Press Release / Media Release - Press Release

NSE:POONAWALLA.name: Poonawalla Fincorp Ltd
NSE:POONAWALLA.businessSummary: Cyrus Poonawalla Group-controlled NBFC (formerly Magma Fincorp) focused on prime-customer consumer and MSME lending — personal, business, vehicle, gold and property loans — with a secured:unsecured mix of roughly 40:60.

notes.announcementTitle: Information Under Regulation 30 ... R/W Schedule A of Reg. 8 of SEBI (Prohibition Of Insider Trading) Regulations 2015
notes.insight: Poonawalla Fincorp disclosed provisional Q1FY27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026) operating metrics: AUM of approximately ₹67,000 crore and liquidity of approximately ₹4,000 crore, both explicitly flagged as provisional and subject to limited review by statutory auditors. No prior notes exist for this company, so YoY/QoQ AUM growth cannot be benchmarked from internal data; ₹67,000cr is a large scale for the NBFC but the filing itself gives no growth rate, NIM, asset quality, or disbursement figures — it is a thin pre-results teaser, not a full result. Direction is neutral-to-mildly positive given continued AUM scale and stated liquidity buffer, but low information density limits actionability. Watch for: the full Q1FY27 results (asset quality/GNPA trend given ongoing unsecured lending stress in the NBFC sector) and confirmation these AUM/liquidity numbers hold post-audit.
notes.announcementDescription: General - Intimation under Regulation 30 of SEBI Listing Regulations 2015.

NSE:SATIN.name: Satin Creditcare Network Ltd
NSE:SATIN.businessSummary: RBI-licensed NBFC-MFI (JLG lending model since 2008) serving ~3.3M women borrowers across 29 states/UTs, plus a growing Non-MFI, housing-finance and business-correspondent portfolio.

notes.announcementTitle: Announcement Under Regulation 30 Of SEBI (LODR) Regulations 2015 - Business Update
notes.insight: Satin's Q1FY27 (quarter ended 30 Jun 2026) business update shows broad-based improvement: consolidated AUM grew ~27% YoY to ~₹16,000cr (₹12,499cr in Q1FY26, +5% QoQ from ₹15,174cr) and standalone AUM grew ~22% YoY to ~₹13,400cr (₹10,956cr in Q1FY26, +4% QoQ). Disbursements jumped 54% YoY to ₹3,453cr consolidated (₹2,242cr in Q1FY26) and 45% YoY to ₹3,003cr standalone. Asset quality improved sharply — credit cost fell to 2.5-3.0% (vs 6.0% in Q1FY26 and inside FY27 guidance of 3.0-3.5%) and GNPA improved to 2.0-2.5% from 3.7%, with X-bucket collection efficiency at ~99.9%; this matters because Indian microfinance has been under stress from over-leveraging/asset-quality concerns over the past year, so a credit-cost halving YoY is a meaningful positive divergence. Non-MFI share rose to 19% of book (from 14%), continuing the diversification-away-from-pure-MFI trend, and the company added 53 branches (network now 1,867 standalone/2,045 consolidated) including a new entry into Kerala. No prior notes exist to check consistency, but management explicitly frames this as 'strongest-ever Q1' — watch the upcoming full results/concall for confirmation these provisional numbers hold and for updated FY27 credit-cost guidance given performance is already tracking below the guided range.
notes.announcementDescription: General - Announcement under Regulation 30 of SEBI (LODR) Regulations 2015 - Business Update

NSE:DIACABS.name: Diamond Power Infrastructure Ltd
NSE:DIACABS.businessSummary: Vadodara-based integrated manufacturer of HT/LT/EHV power cables and T&D conductors (aluminium/alloy wire rods, ACSR/AAAC conductors) plus transmission towers, serving power, data-center, infra, defence and renewables customers in India and export markets.

notes.announcementTitle: Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Press Release / Media Release
notes.insight: Diamond Power Infrastructure secured a Rs. 435.71 crore order (exclusive of GST) for ~21.35 lakh meters of HT & LT power cables (HT: 1,89,404m; LT: 19,45,920m) for the 310 MW HYD22-HYD26 Data Center Projects at Hyderabad, to be executed by L&T, Sterling & Wilson and Blue Star — all top-tier EPC/data-center infrastructure contractors. Deliveries run first week of August 2026 to March 2027 (~8 months execution), implying roughly ₹163 crore/quarter of run-rate revenue from this single order alone (435.71 ÷ 8 × 3), pricing is variable per the IEEMA PV formula off April 2026 indices so realized value can move with input costs. This is explicitly framed by the company as 'among the larger single cable supply orders in India's data centre segment' and taps the high-growth data-center capex theme; no related-party or promoter interest is involved, and the order is in the ordinary course of business at arm's length. No prior notes or trailing revenue figures exist for this company yet, so the order's true book-to-bill/percent-of-revenue impact can't be computed here — treat this as flagged for verification against DIACABS's last annual/quarterly revenue once available. Watch for: whether this order is booked incrementally in coming quarterly results and any follow-on orders from the same Hyderabad data-center cluster.
